questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the basic economic questions that every economic system must answer?

options.text: How should the goods be produced?
For whom should the goods be produced?
Which government agency should collect taxes?

questions.explanation: The three basic questions all concern the allocation of scarce resources: what, how and for whom. Choosing a tax-collecting agency is an administrative matter that arises after those allocation decisions have been made.

distractorRationale.a: This is the first basic question — the composition of output
distractorRationale.b: This is the second basic question — the technique of production
distractorRationale.c: This is the third basic question — the distribution of output

questions.stem: An economic system in which the means of production are privately owned and prices are determined by the forces of demand and supply is called
questions.explanation: Private ownership plus allocation by the price mechanism are the two defining marks of capitalism, also called a free enterprise or laissez-faire economy.

distractorRationale.b: Socialism rests on state ownership and central planning, the opposite of both features
distractorRationale.c: A subsistence economy produces mainly for the producer's own use, with little exchange at all
distractorRationale.d: A command economy allocates by directive from a planning authority, not by prices

questions.stem: In a purely socialist economy, resources are allocated mainly through

options.text: the free interaction of demand and supply

questions.explanation: Since the state owns the means of production in a socialist economy, a planning authority must decide output targets, input allocation and prices. The price mechanism plays little or no allocating role.

distractorRationale.a: Free demand and supply allocation is the hallmark of capitalism
distractorRationale.c: Private firms scarcely exist, so competition among them cannot be the allocator
distractorRationale.d: Allocation by custom describes a traditional economy, not a planned socialist one

questions.stem: Nigeria is described as a mixed economy because

options.text: it produces both agricultural and industrial goods
both private individuals and government own and control means of production
it trades with both African and European countries
both the naira and foreign currencies circulate in the country

questions.explanation: The word mixed refers to the mixture of ownership and control, not to a mixture of products, partners or currencies. In Nigeria private firms operate for profit while government owns refineries, universities and transmission infrastructure and regulates the private sector.

distractorRationale.a: Almost every economy produces both farm and factory output, so this does not identify the system
distractorRationale.c: The pattern of trading partners has nothing to do with ownership of resources
distractorRationale.d: Currency circulation is a monetary matter, not a question of who owns the means of production

questions.stem: A major disadvantage of a capitalist economy is that

options.text: consumers have very little choice of goods
income and wealth become very unequally distributed
there is no incentive for individuals to work hard
prices are fixed by a central planning authority

questions.explanation: Because rewards under capitalism follow ownership of property and marketable skill, those who start with capital accumulate more while those without it fall behind. Unprofitable but socially necessary services also tend to be neglected.

distractorRationale.a: Capitalism normally widens consumer choice; restricted choice is a criticism of central planning
distractorRationale.c: The profit motive supplies a strong work incentive; weak incentives are a socialist criticism
distractorRationale.d: Central price fixing is a feature of a command economy, not of capitalism

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the role of the price mechanism in a free enterprise economy?

options.text: It guarantees that every citizen receives an equal share of national income
It signals what consumers want and rations scarce goods among competing buyers
It removes the problem of scarcity from the economy
It enables government to fix fair prices for essential commodities

questions.explanation: A rising price does two jobs at once: it tells producers that consumers want more of a good and it discourages the buyers who value it least, so the limited supply goes to those willing to pay. This signalling and rationing function is why no central planner is needed.

distractorRationale.a: The price mechanism distributes income according to ownership and productivity, which produces inequality rather than equality
distractorRationale.c: No mechanism can abolish scarcity; prices only help society cope with it
distractorRationale.d: Government price fixing suspends the price mechanism instead of expressing it

questions.stem: Privatisation increases the role of the private sector in an economy.
questions.explanation: True. Privatisation transfers ownership of state enterprises to private investors, as Nigeria did with the power distribution companies in 2013, so the share of activity in private hands rises. Commercialisation, by contrast, keeps state ownership but makes the enterprise run on business lines.

distractorRationale.b: This confuses privatisation with nationalisation, which moves assets in the opposite direction

questions.stem: Select the TWO features that belong to a socialist economy.

options.text: Private ownership of the major means of production
Profit as the main motive for production
State ownership of the major means of production
Free competition among many independent firms

questions.explanation: Socialism is identified by state ownership of the major means of production and by a central plan that replaces the price mechanism as the allocator of resources. Everything else follows from those two features.

distractorRationale.a: Private ownership is the defining feature of capitalism
distractorRationale.c: The profit motive drives capitalist production; socialism claims social welfare as its motive
distractorRationale.e: Free competition presupposes many private firms, which socialism does not permit

questions.stem: Which of the following is one of the three basic economic questions every economic system must answer?
questions.explanation: Every economic system must address what to produce, how to produce it, and for whom the goods and services are produced. These questions are fundamental to understanding the allocation of resources in any economy.

distractorRationale.a: While 'What to produce?' is a basic question, it is not the only one.
distractorRationale.b: This question is important, but there are more questions that need to be answered.
distractorRationale.c: This is one of the three questions, but not the complete answer.

questions.stem: Which economic system is characterized by collective ownership of resources?
questions.explanation: Socialism is an economic system where the means of production are owned collectively or by the state. This contrasts with capitalism, where private ownership is prevalent.

distractorRationale.a: Capitalism is based on private ownership, not collective ownership.
distractorRationale.c: A mixed economy incorporates elements of both capitalism and socialism.
distractorRationale.d: Traditional economies are based on customs and do not primarily focus on ownership structures.

questions.stem: In a mixed economy, which of the following best describes the role of the government?

options.text: The government controls all economic activities.
The government regulates and intervenes in the economy.
The government only focuses on taxation.

questions.explanation: In a mixed economy, the government plays a significant role by regulating and intervening in the economy to promote social welfare and prevent market failures. This is a key feature that distinguishes mixed economies from purely capitalist or socialist systems.

distractorRationale.a: This statement is incorrect as the government does play a role in mixed economies.
distractorRationale.b: This describes a socialist economy rather than a mixed one.
distractorRationale.d: While taxation is important, it is not the only focus of government in a mixed economy.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes capitalism?
questions.explanation: Capitalism is characterized by private ownership of the means of production, where individuals and businesses own resources and operate for profit. This system encourages competition and innovation.

distractorRationale.a: This describes socialism, not capitalism.
distractorRationale.c: Equal distribution of wealth is more aligned with socialist principles.
distractorRationale.d: Central planning is a feature of socialist economies.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a key feature of a mixed economy?
questions.explanation: A mixed economy features both private and public sectors that coexist and collaborate. This allows for a balance between free market principles and government intervention to address social needs.

distractorRationale.a: Complete government control is characteristic of socialism, not a mixed economy.
distractorRationale.c: A mixed economy involves some level of government intervention.
distractorRationale.d: Monopolies are typically discouraged in mixed economies to promote competition.

questions.stem: What is one major advantage of socialism compared to capitalism?
questions.explanation: One major advantage of socialism is that it aims for an equitable distribution of resources, reducing income inequality and providing basic needs for all citizens. This contrasts with capitalism, which can lead to greater disparities in wealth.

distractorRationale.a: Socialism seeks to reduce income inequality, not increase it.
distractorRationale.c: Higher levels of competition are typically a feature of capitalism.
distractorRationale.d: Greater consumer choice is more characteristic of a capitalist economy.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of capitalism?
questions.explanation: Central planning is not a characteristic of capitalism; rather, capitalism is defined by market-driven forces where decisions are made by individuals and businesses rather than centralized authorities.

distractorRationale.a: The profit motive is a fundamental aspect of capitalism.
distractorRationale.b: Private property is a key feature of capitalist economies.
distractorRationale.d: Competition is essential in capitalism to drive innovation and efficiency.

questions.stem: How does a mixed economy address the issue of unemployment?

options.text: Through government intervention and job creation programs
By reducing taxes on corporations only

questions.explanation: In a mixed economy, the government can intervene in the labor market through policies and programs aimed at creating jobs and reducing unemployment. This can include public works projects and incentives for businesses to hire.

distractorRationale.a: Eliminating private businesses would not address unemployment effectively.
distractorRationale.c: Allowing only private enterprises would not provide the necessary intervention needed to combat unemployment.
distractorRationale.d: Reducing taxes on corporations may not directly lead to job creation.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements best describes Nigeria's economic system?

options.text: It is a mixed economy with both private and public sectors.
It has no defined economic system.

questions.explanation: Nigeria operates as a mixed economy, where both private enterprises and government entities play significant roles in the economy. This structure allows for a blend of market-driven and planned economic activities.

distractorRationale.a: Nigeria's economy is not purely capitalist due to significant government involvement.
distractorRationale.b: It is not purely socialist as there is a strong private sector.
distractorRationale.d: Nigeria has a defined economic system that incorporates elements of both capitalism and socialism.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a disadvantage of socialism?
questions.explanation: A common disadvantage of socialism is the lack of consumer choice, as the government often controls the production of goods and services. This can lead to a limited variety of products available for consumers compared to capitalist economies.

distractorRationale.a: Reduced income inequality is generally seen as an advantage of socialism.
distractorRationale.c: Increased competition is typically associated with capitalism.
distractorRationale.d: Higher profits for businesses are more characteristic of a capitalist system.

questions.stem: What is a key reason for Nigeria's classification as a mixed economy?

options.text: Complete government control over all industries
Existence of both private and public sectors

questions.explanation: Nigeria is classified as a mixed economy because it has both private and public sectors that interact and influence the economic landscape. This allows for diverse economic activities and resource allocation.

distractorRationale.a: Complete government control would indicate a socialist economy, not a mixed one.
distractorRationale.c: A mixed economy involves some level of government regulation.
distractorRationale.d: Nigeria's economy is diverse and not solely reliant on agriculture.

questions.stem: Which of the following best illustrates the concept of 'invisible hand' in a capitalist economy?
questions.explanation: The 'invisible hand' refers to the self-regulating nature of the marketplace where producers and consumers interact freely, leading to efficient resource allocation. This concept is central to capitalism.

distractorRationale.a: Government regulation interferes with market dynamics.
distractorRationale.c: Social welfare programs are indicative of socialist principles.
distractorRationale.d: Public ownership contradicts capitalist ideology.

questions.stem: In a capitalist system, which of the following is most likely to determine the prices of goods?

distractorRationale.a: Government intervention disrupts market forces.
distractorRationale.c: Fixed pricing does not reflect true market conditions.
distractorRationale.d: Consumer preferences alone cannot dictate prices without supply considerations.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements accurately compares capitalism and socialism?

options.text: Capitalism prioritizes individual profit while socialism prioritizes collective welfare.

Capitalism is characterized by equal distribution of wealth.

questions.explanation: Capitalism emphasizes individual profits and private ownership, whereas socialism focuses on collective welfare and often involves government ownership of key resources. This fundamental difference shapes how each system operates.

distractorRationale.c: Capitalism does not guarantee equal distribution of wealth; it often leads to wealth disparity.
